title: structured_extract output
description: Output for structured_extract. `extraction` is null when the engine returned no call, and that is a REPORTED outcome rather than an error: a document with none of the requested fields is a legitimate answer. When the engine did return an object, the package re-validates it against the caller's schema and publishes every violation in `issues` instead of discarding the attempt — the caller decides whether a partially grounded extraction is usable.

extraction.description: The extracted record, verbatim from the engine. Null when no call was returned; never an empty object standing in for a failure.

proposed.description: Whether the engine returned a call at all. False is the honest report of 'nothing matched'.

valid.description: Whether `extraction` satisfies the caller's schema. A constrained grammar makes the object well-formed, which is not the same as correct.

issues.description: Every violation of the caller's schema, so a partial extraction is visible rather than silently accepted.

reasoning.description: The engine's own account of the turn.

grounding.description: The engine's grounding report. `negation` true means the model believes the input NEGATES the record, which a caller must not read as a positive extraction.

meta.description: The host stamps this envelope. The provider never authors it (EXT-17).
